themes_detail.label: Street Noise Surge
themes_detail.summary: Noise complaints from streets and sidewalks spiked to 35 this week versus a 7.5 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—a 367% increase (z-score: 10.79)—suggesting a sudden, localized disruption affecting Flatbush/PLG residents THIS WEEK.
evidence: 35 street/sidewalk noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 7.5 weekly average (z-score: 10.79)
367% spike from baseline suggests acute event or condition, not chronic issue
High statistical significance indicates real pattern, not random variation
reporting_angles: What construction, street activity, or event triggered the noise surge this week?
Interview affected residents along high-complaint corridors to identify the source

themes_detail.label: Street Sweeping & Litter Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Street sweeping complaints jumped to 11 THIS WEEK (1367% above the 0.8 weekly baseline), and litter basket complaints remain severely elevated at 5 complaints 3 weeks ago versus 0.1 baseline—indicating a potential sanitation workforce gap or service collapse in Flatbush/PLG.
evidence: Street sweeping complaints: 11 THIS WEEK vs. 0.8 weekly average (z-score: 12.36, +1367%)
Litter basket complaints: 5 complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.1 average (z-score: 14.74, +3900%)
Dirty condition complaints also elevated: 52 last week vs. 22.4 average (+132%)
reporting_angles: Is Sanitation having staffing issues or equipment shortages affecting Flatbush/PLG specifically?
Map the geographic clusters of street sweeping complaints to identify underserved blocks or neighborhoods

themes_detail.label: Asbestos & Contamination Spike
themes_detail.summary: Asbestos complaints spiked to 11 last week versus 0.9 weekly average—a 1157% increase (z-score: 7.98)—raising urgent concerns about building safety and potential hazardous material exposure across Flatbush/PLG.
evidence: Asbestos complaints: 11 last week vs. 0.9 weekly average (z-score: 7.98, +1157%)
319 building permits filed in last 90 days (182 alterations) suggest active renovation activity that may be exposing asbestos
Spike coincides with period of construction activity in district
reporting_angles: Which buildings or construction projects triggered the asbestos complaints? Are contractors following EPA removal protocols?
Interview DOB and NYC Health about whether they've identified unsafe renovation practices or contractor violations

themes_detail.label: Dead Trees & Environmental Decline
themes_detail.summary: Dead or dying tree complaints surged to 4 three weeks ago versus 0.1 baseline—a 3100% spike (z-score: 11.72)—paired with ongoing street sweeping and litter complaints, suggesting broader environmental neglect in the neighborhood.
evidence: Dead/dying tree complaints: 4 three weeks ago vs. 0.1 average (z-score: 11.72, +3100%)
Aligns with community board's recurring budget request to 'improve access to parks and amenities'
Converges with street sweeping and litter spikes to suggest Parks Department resource gaps
reporting_angles: Has Parks Department reduced tree maintenance or inspection in Flatbush/PLG?
Which specific blocks or parks have the dead trees? Are residents concerned about canopy loss or pedestrian safety?

themes_detail.label: Police Non-Emergency Complaints Rise
themes_detail.summary: Non-emergency police matter complaints reached 9 three weeks ago versus 2.8 baseline—a 227% spike (z-score: 3.81)—potentially reflecting disorder, street activity, or quality-of-life concerns residents are escalating to law enforcement.
evidence: Non-emergency police complaints: 9 three weeks ago vs. 2.8 weekly average (z-score: 3.81, +227%)
Complaint type lacks specificity; requires follow-up to identify what street conditions triggered calls
Coincides with broader sanitation and noise issues
reporting_angles: What types of non-emergency issues are residents calling police about—loitering, street vending, open-air drug use?
Cross-reference with NYPD precinct crime data to see if there's a pattern beyond 311 complaints
